Rafael,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form. We reviewed with infra and procurement and attached a marked-up PDF (acme_redlines_msa_v2.pdf) plus a maintenance matrix that shows our preferred blackout and notification windows. High-level concerns: 

- Uptime target: we think the order form should specify a single global availability metric (99.95%) and an explicit measurement window rather than per-region aggregation.
- Service credits: the current draft's formula is ambiguous for multi-region incidents and for rolling maintenance that impacts only one region. We need language that ties credits to customer-visible availability, and a clear example calculation.
- Response times: the P1/P2 definitions are close but we need confirmation that the initial response begins at detection, not triage completion.
- Maintenance windows & ownership: we need crisp rules about planned maintenance notifications (min 72 hours), emergency maintenance carve-outs, and which party owns failover coordination when Redwood triggers cross-region fallback.

Please see acme_redlines_msa_v2.pdf and maintenance_matrix.csv for inline comments. We are available for a short call Wednesday or Thursday to walk through the contentious points.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
VP, Infrastructure
Acme Tech

Laura — appreciate the detailed redlines and the matrix. Quick notes from our side before we align Legal and SRE: 

- Measurement & aggregation: We are open to a single customer-visible metric (99.95%) measured at the account level. We need to confirm how we attribute partial regional degradations (e.g., 1 of 3 regions degraded) — suggested approach: weight by traffic % per region for the customer. Karthik, can Ops confirm feasibility and telemetry for weighted availability?

- Credits: Marissa, please advise on capping credits (customer request currently pushes toward uncapped remedies). We typically cap at 100% of the monthly invoice but can discuss a structured ladder tied to outage minutes.

- Response SLAs: We accept clarifying that initial acknowledgement is measured from detection/ingress of the customer incident report or the first automated alert on our side, whichever comes first. We will propose explicit wording.

- Maintenance: We can agree to 72h notice for planned maintenance that will affect customer-visible availability. For emergency maintenance we will follow an emergency carve-out but commit to post-incident reporting within 24 hours. Ownership for cross-region failover: Redwood will own the execution of managed failover when the root cause is within our control; we request joint runbooks and a single point-of-contact for coordinated cutovers.

Attached: redlines_commentary.docx — Marissa and I added high-level legal positions and suggested alternate language for the credit formula.

Next step: Marissa — can you put together a short redline that keeps the credit ceiling option open but proposes a two-tier ladder? Karthik — please reply with a short ops note on weighted regional availability and how we would calculate it. Laura — are you free Thursday 11/12 at 10:00 PT for a 30-minute sync?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Team — quick internal legal take before the call. Quoting Rafael's message below for context.

On measurement & credits:
- We should avoid an uncapped credit exposure. Proposed compromise: cap credits at 100% of the monthly invoice for any 30-day measurement period, but allow for an exception tied to gross negligence (narrowly defined) subject to escalation.
- Insert example calculation in the order form appendix showing weighted regional impact (we can draft the example; Rafael can embed Karthik's numbers).

On maintenance & notice:
- Planned maintenance: require >=72 hours notice for any maintenance expected to affect customer-visible availability. Notice may be shortened by mutual written agreement.
- Emergency maintenance: define as an action necessary to prevent imminent, material impact to service or data; carve out with commitment to post-incident incident report and remediation timeline within 24 hours.

On response times and acknowledgements:
- Define "initial acknowledgement" as the time Redwood logs the issue in its incident tracker or confirms receipt of a customer support API call/webhook. Do not tie to triage resolution.
- P1: initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes, continuous phone/IM handoff until mitigation. P2: initial acknowledgement within 2 business hours. These are normative suggestions — ops may prefer slightly different numbers.

I will draft the legal redline with: (1) concrete credit cap language, (2) the appendix example, and (3) explicit maintenance categories and notice windows. Sharing a redline file shortly.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
